## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D multiplayer battle royale shooter inspired by Free Fire, with polished gameplay and Android-friendly controls and performance.

## Requirements
- Include realistic weapons, smooth controls, multiple maps, online multiplayer, customization, game modes, vehicles, survival mechanics, high-quality graphics, and an intuitive UI.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) for checks and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Assistant chose to build a standalone Three.js game with procedural graphics and audio, desktop and touch controls, and local AI bots.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the UI shell, styles, game configuration, utilities, audio, profile persistence, procedural models, world generation, effects, input, player controller, bot AI, HUD, and match controller.
- Added local Three.js and font assets.

### Active
- Finish the application entry point and connect the lobby, game, settings, and UI.
- Run the game, resolve errors, test playability and responsive controls, and capture a screenshot.

### Blocked
- Online multiplayer is not implemented in the work shown; multiplayer is currently represented by local bots.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current files and implement the missing app entry point and UI wiring.
2. Run the project and fix runtime or gameplay issues.
3. Verify desktop and mobile layouts/controls; capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize implemented features and limitations, including local-only multiplayer.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI structure and module import map.
- `css/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `js/config.js`: game modes, weapons, maps, and profile defaults.
- `js/world.js`: procedural world and map construction.
- `js/player.js`: player movement, camera, and weapon handling.
- `js/bots.js`: local bot AI and match population.
- `js/hud.js`: in-match HUD and results.
- `js/game.js`: match lifecycle and gameplay controller.
- `js/input.js`: keyboard, mouse, and touch controls.
- `js/models.js`: procedural character, weapon, and vehicle models.
- `js/effects.js`: combat effects.
- `js/profile.js`: profile persistence and customization.
- `js/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio sound effects.
- `js/utils.js`: shared math and rendering utilities.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: locally bundled Three.js.
- `assets/fonts/`: locally bundled UI fonts.

## Important Context
- Assistant created the files using large write operations; no test run, screenshot, or validation is shown.
- The latest shown work ends immediately after creating `js/game.js`; app bootstrap and integration remain unverified.

## Objective
- Finish the existing standalone 3D battle royale game: wire up the lobby and match UI, then validate gameplay and responsive controls.
- The intended game includes Android-friendly controls and multiplayer-inspired features; the implementation currently uses local bots rather than online multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing project and make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) for checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with procedural graphics and audio, desktop and touch controls, and local AI bots.
- Multiplayer is not implemented online; current matches use bots.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `js/main.js` to bootstrap the app, render the lobby, wire UI, manage settings and match lifecycle, and run the render loop.
- Fixed startup issues found during browser testing: missing `Input.clearListeners()`, early HUD access to player state, and collider format handling in `rayAABB`.
- Added safer spawn selection and a mouse-lock hint; fixed TDM kill score updates and result/death callbacks after match disposal.
- Ran syntax checks and browser smoke tests. The lobby populated, and a match started with bots and active HUD.
- Captured and inspected JPEG screenshots at `/tmp/opencode/shots/lobby-1.jpg` and `/tmp/opencode/shots/match-2.jpg`.

### Active
- Continue testing the match, inspect any remaining runtime errors, and improve performance or controls as needed.
- Verify mobile layout and touch controls; browser checks so far used a 1280×800 desktop viewport.

### Blocked
- Online multiplayer remains unimplemented; gameplay is local-only.

## Next Move
1. Re-run the browser smoke test and inspect complete console/exception output after the collider fix.
2. Test shooting, movement, pause/results, settings, and touch controls across lobby and match.
3. Inspect only the newest screenshot after any recapture; check desktop and mobile layouts.
4. Summarize the finished features and clearly note local-only multiplayer.

## Relevant Files
- `js/main.js`: application bootstrap, lobby scene, UI wiring, settings, and render loop.
- `js/game.js`: match lifecycle and gameplay controller.
- `js/input.js`: desktop and touch controls.
- `js/hud.js`: in-match HUD, pause, and results.
- `js/bots.js`: local bot AI and match population.
- `js/world.js`: procedural maps and world collision/raycast helpers.
- `js/player.js`: movement, camera, and weapon handling.
- `js/utils.js`: shared math and ray/AABB helper.
- `index.html`: UI structure and module import map.
- `css/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `/tmp/opencode/shots/match-2.jpg`: latest captured match screenshot to inspect if a newer one has not been captured.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The browser smoke test reached active play, with 17 bots, 50 alive, and the HUD visible; reported performance was around 21 FPS in the test environment.
- Browser logs included audio autoplay warnings; review the full post-fix console output for any remaining exceptions.
